messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: p99 decode latency spike > 6s in us-east-1 on model-serving pool 'decode-prod-01'. Streaming stalls detected. Auto-escalation to eng-oncall. Link: https://alerts.redwood.example/alert/1851234567 :rotating_light:

alice_oncall: I'm on it. seeing the alert — starting basic triage. tagging runtime + sre.

ben_runtime: pinged, pulling traces now. any recent kernel/compile rollouts?

chuck_sre: I saw a small kernel patch roll earlier today to enable new TRT flash kernel optimizations. rollout id: rollout-2026-03-08-trtflash-v2. Noted a couple build warnings but passed e2e.

alice_oncall: ok — initial metrics: p95 from 220ms -> 420ms, p99 from 1.2s -> 6.4s across decode endpoints. streaming stall count (stream_token_gap > 200ms) jumped x8. Looks like tail & streaming stalls, not errors. No obvious increase in 5xx.

dana_eng: thanks. can someone run PromQL for minor/major pagefaults for the host pool and GPU memcpy times? suspecting pinned-memory behaviour after kernel change.

ben_runtime: running queries:
```
sum by(instance) (rate(node_vm_minor_pagefaults_total{job="nodes",env="prod",region="us-east-1"}[5m]))
sum by(instance) (rate(container_cpu_user_seconds_total{job="kube",container="decode-runtime"}[5m]))
avg_over_time(redis_kv_cache_hit_rate[15m])
```
Early result: minor pagefaults spiked ~x10 on affected hosts starting at 1851234500. GPU memcpy tail times (from tracer) show percentiles pushed up at >95th.

chuck_sre: looking at dmesg from one host: repeated WARN about "non-paged memory fallback" and some DMA mapping retries. Could be that new kernel's page pinning API changed behaviour under heavy readahead/caching — leads to brief page stalls when runtime tries to pin large KV cache buffers.

nora_support: received a support ping from customer AcmeAnalytics — reports streaming responses stalling mid-stream (long pauses between chunks). They noticed increase ~30m ago.

alice_oncall: customer impact: we have ~6 customers on the affected pool; AcmeAnalytics, BioGenX, ChattyInc flagged. No 5xx but UX will be bad. marking Sev=2 for now, because degraded latency impacting SLAs.

ben_runtime: quick mitigation plan options:
- roll back kernel update on affected hosts (risky, needs infra windows)
- change routing to move traffic off decode-prod-01 to decode-prod-02 (older kernel) — faster, less risky
- force runtime to use "compat kernel" codepath (env var flip) to avoid the new pinned allocation path
- reduce batch size / enable fast-respond mode to bypass KV-cache heavy codepath

Which should we do now?

chuck_sre: routing change is the fastest. infra can shift k8s service weights. I'll coordinate with infra to shift 50% immediately and ramp if it improves.

dana_eng: we have an env var RUNTIME_FORCE_LEGACY_PIN=1 that avoids the new pinned allocation in the newest runtime binary; it's supported without restart (reads on next request) for a subset of callers. We can flip for the service via config rollout. That would avoid kernel path entirely.

alice_oncall: do that in parallel: 1) infra shift 50% to decode-prod-02, 2) config flip RUNTIME_FORCE_LEGACY_PIN=1 for decode-prod-01, 3) increase warm-up traffic to refill KV cache on decode-prod-02.

ben_runtime: applying config flip now for decode-prod-01 (canary to 10% first). posting rollout command:
```
kubectl set env deployment/decode-runtime RUNTIME_FORCE_LEGACY_PIN=1 -n prod --record
```
Will watch metrics.

chuck_sre: infra: shifting weights now. command sent to router:
```
/api/v1/routesets/decode/shift?from=decode-prod-01&to=decode-prod-02&percent=50
```
Router acked.

alice_oncall: monitoring. initial after 3m: p99 dropped from 6.4s -> 2.1s on decode-prod-02 traffic. decode-prod-01 still high at 5.8s but canary flip looks promising.

dana_eng: can we bump canary to 50% for the env var? the legacy pin path is safe but we should watch CPU.

ben_runtime: increasing to 50% now. watching traces and logs.

nora_support: AcmeAnalytics reports improvement, streaming gaps now much smaller.

alice_oncall: good. continue ramp. also need to capture heap dumps / pinned allocation counters for postmortem. ben — can you collect runtime diagnostics from affected pods (pinned_alloc_count, mmap stats) and upload to S3 / link?

ben_runtime: on it. commands used:
```
kubectl exec -it pod/decode-runtime-xyz -- sh -c 'cat /proc/vmstat | egrep "pgpgin|pgmajfault|pgfault"'
kubectl exec -it pod/decode-runtime-xyz -- curl -s http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep pinned_alloc
```
Uploaded to s3: s3://redwood-incidents/1851234567/diag.tar.gz

chuck_sre: infra will keep routing shift until metrics stable for 20m. We should open a rollback ticket for the kernel patch (rollout-2026-03-08-trtflash-v2) and coordinate with QA to reproduce.

dana_eng: will reproduce in staging by re-applying the kernel patch and running our decode stress harness with streaming enabled and KV cache warm population. Assigning to me.

alice_oncall: action items so far:
- chuck: keep routing shift + monitor (in progress)
- ben: gather diagnostics and keep rolling config canary (in progress)
- dana: reproduce in staging and root-cause the pinned allocation interaction (in progress)
- nora: notify affected customers with ETA (in progress)

eva_pm: please add customer impact summary for execs: estimated affected API keys, minutes of SLO breach, and mitigation timeline.

nora_support: messaging going out: "We're aware of streaming stalls for some customers in us-east-1, mitigation in progress, switching traffic to healthy pool. We'll follow up with timeline and workaround. Apologies for the interruption."

alice_oncall: status @ 1851234700: p99 overall down to 1.8s, streaming stall rate back to baseline for >70% traffic. Keeping Sev=2 until fully recovered.

ben_runtime: can confirm pinned_alloc counters dropped after legacy pin flip. no more DMA mapping retries in dmesg on those hosts. Uploading logs and stack traces to the same S3 bundle.

chuck_sre: decision: do not rollback kernel cluster-wide for now. keep routing + env var flip as mitigation. We'll schedule a rollback/patch fix after reproduction and QA.

dana_eng: preliminary root cause hypothesis: new TRT/FlashAttention kernel used a different pinned memory allocation pattern that assumed contiguous pinned buffers; under our large KV cache sizes it triggered extra kernel DMA mapping calls that cause short-lived page pin/unpin cycles, producing userland stalls during memcpy. The compile flag that changed behavior was -DBT_PINNED_OPT=ON in the TRT build.

alice_oncall: thanks. I'll prepare a short incident note and assign postmortem owner. who wants to own the postmortem? dana or ben?

ben_runtime: I can take postmortem on runtime side (query perf traces, remediation steps). dana can cover interaction with kernel/trt. Let's co-own.

eva_pm: I'll prepare customer-facing summary once postmortem draft is ready.

alice_oncall: handing off to oncall shift: tomorrow's oncall (chuck) will continue monitoring for 6h and confirm we can remove routing shift and env var flip after staging fix. Handoff notes:
- mitigations applied: routing shift to decode-prod-02, RUNTIME_FORCE_LEGACY_PIN toggled to 50% -> 100% on decode-prod-01, KV cache warmups performed.
- diagnostics uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/1851234567/diag.tar.gz
- affected customers: AcmeAnalytics, BioGenX, ChattyInc (+3 smaller tenants)
- tentative root cause: TRT flash kernel pinned allocation pattern + compile flag -DBT_PINNED_OPT=ON
- next steps: reproduce in staging, prepare kernel patch rollback plan or TRT recompile with compat flag, QA verification, schedule cluster patch OR merge in runtime fallback permanently.

chuck_sre: acknowledged handoff. I'll watch between 1851234720 and 1851250000 and will escalate if regression.

alice_oncall: closing pager for now — system stabilized under mitigation. Postmortem owners: ben_runtime + dana_eng. Please include timeline, mitigation commands, customer impact, and a remediation plan (kernel patch roll or permanent runtime fallback).

nora_support: I'll follow up with impacted customers with recovery note + workaround.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Sev2 incident 1851234567 resolved to mitigated state. Tags: paging, kernel, trt-flashattention, latency, streaming-stalls.

alice_oncall: thanks everyone.
